stem: Which of the following equations, together with \(\frac{x}{2} - \frac{y}{6} = 1\), forms a system of linear equations with no solution?
solution: Multiply the given equation by 6: \(3x - y = 6\), or \(y = 3x - 6\).
A system has no solution when the lines are parallel and distinct: same slope, different \(y\)-intercept.
\(6x - 2y = 3\) becomes \(y = 3x - \frac{3}{2}\): slope 3, intercept \(-\frac{3}{2} \ne -6\). This is the one.
\(9x - 3y = 18\) is the same line (infinitely many solutions); the other two have different slopes (one solution).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This equation is 18 times the given one, so it describes the same line: infinitely many solutions, not none.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This line has slope \(-3\), not 3; the lines cross, so there is exactly one solution.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This line has slope \(\frac{1}{3}\), the reciprocal of 3; the lines cross, so there is exactly one solution.
explanation.D: Correct. This line is \(y = 3x - \frac{3}{2}\), parallel to \(y = 3x - 6\) but distinct, so the system has no solution.

verify:
x, y = symbols('x y')
g = x/2 - y/6 - 1
f = lambda s: value(s.split('=')[0]) - value(s.split('=')[1])
none = [k for k in choices if solve([g, f(choices[k])], [x, y]) == []]
assert none == [answer]
assert simplify(f(choices['A']) - 18*g) == 0
